title: Vocalion recording session in Chicago: 'Lazy Rhythm'
summary: The band travels to Chicago to record its theme 'Lazy Rhythm' and 'I Like Pie, I Like Cake' and others, with Blanton and Floyd Smith solos and listed personnel.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Every night on the job, man, he was just terrific. He just -- he was just out of this world. So, that summer, getting back to Mugs Roberts, when we decided to go to Chicago and make those recordings Jimmy Blanton was with us during the time and in the personnel of that band that made those recordings there was George Hudson, Crack Stanley and Merle (unintelligible) am I right?
And a boy on trombone named Johnny Orange. On the saxophone was my brother Charles, myself, Jeter
Francis Whitney, from Oklahoma. And he was a great saxophonist, wasn't he?

A great musician. So, we made our theme song, 'Lazy Rhythm,' and we made 'I Like Pie, I Like Cake.' On the opposite side. Jimmy Blanton had a solo; he had a eight-bar solo, I think it was, a little interlude, you remember?
Floyd Smith had a solo on the channel of 'Lazy Rhythm.'
Didn't we do -- didn't we do 'Make-Believe,' too, to Ted Smith sing.
'Make Believe' and 'I'll Always Be In Love With You.'
So the band made those recordings and we came on back to Chicago. We didn't play Chicago, that time Charles?
